elements.label: Workday 'Add, Edit, or Delete Version' app window (whole UI frame)

elements.manual_reason: No candidate box isolates the Version Details form; it scrolls back to the top (General / Access Control) inside its pane during the pull-out.
elements.label: Version Details form scrolling back to top

elements.manual_reason: No candidate box covers the mouse cursor, which ends over the save icon in the Version Details toolbar.
elements.label: Mouse cursor moving to the save icon

pattern.description: Reverse of a UI camera push-in: a virtual camera pulls out from a close-up of the settings form to reveal the full app window on the brand-blue backdrop, while the form scrolls back to its top and the cursor heads to Save.
pattern.why_premium: A smooth eased zoom-out re-establishes context after a detail close-up instead of a hard cut, so the viewer sees where the edited settings live before the save action.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.fromTo(appWindow, {scale: 1.45, x: -180, y: -260}, {scale: 1, x: 0, y: 0, duration: 1.0, ease: 'power2.inOut', transformOrigin: '50% 50%'}); in the same timeline at 0 tween form scrollTop back to 0 (duration 0.6, 'power2.out') and the cursor to the save icon (duration 0.8, 'power1.inOut').
build_hint.remotion: const p = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); scale = interpolate(p, [0, 1], [1.45, 1]); translate x/y from the zoom focus to 0 with the same p; form translateY and cursor position driven by separate interpolates.

notes: Camera verdict is pull_out; taxonomy has no pull-out pattern so ui_camera_push_in (reversed) is the closest. The in-pane form scroll during the zoom is inferred from the filmstrip and could be a reflow instead.
